raw_case_text:
A 44-years-old female patient was referred to Istanbul University-Cerrahpasa, Istanbul, Turkey in 2020 with a mass in her right thigh which was present in a smaller diameter for ten years. She did not seek any healthcare for her mass until the mass got larger in diameter during the last few months. Four months before, the patient was also diagnosed with liver CE as a result of abdominal ultrasonography (USG) and computed tomography (CT). Multiple cysts between 20-50 mm in size were found in the right lobe of the liver, located in segment.
The patient underwent surgery and after partial cystectomy and germinative membrane dissection, the cavitary area was washed with povidone-iodine and the patient received albendazole treatment in the postoperative period. Before the index surgery, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the thigh was also made to evaluate the mass in her right thigh. The MRI showed a lesion with a size of 180x100x75 mm consisting of cystic components within the right vastus lateralis muscle (Fig. 1). The patient did not show the result of MRI to any physician and she just continued her follow-ups for her excised liver CE. After the patient recovered and completed her albendazole treatment (three 1-month oral doses (10 mg/kg/d) separated by 14-day intervals), she applied to our clinic for her thigh mass. A new MRI was ordered and a mass of 150x70x55 mm was detected along proximal and middle one-third of her right thigh. The complete blood count and biochemical tests were within normal limits. The surgical excision of the mass was planned. The patient had already received albendazole treatment for 3 months preoperatively, after her liver CE surgery.
The mass was reached by a 20 cm longitudinal skin incision on the right thigh anterolaterally. Total excision was performed without damaging the cyst membrane. The surgical area was washed, the incision was closed through a hemovac drain. The mass was sent to pathology and the result was compatible with CE. In the macroscopic examination of the removed cyst, daughter cysts were seen and it was found that the hydatid sand structure was denser and more caseified than normal (Fig. 2). The patient continued to use 10 mg/kg/d albendazole for two months in the postoperative period with the recommendation of the infectious diseases department.
The comparison of MRI sections showed that albendazole eliminated the vesicle structures by accelerating the degeneration process of the cyst and created a heterogeneous unilocular encapsulated cyst structure compared to the previous multilocular appearance. According to the WHO-IWGE classification, the grade of CE appearance changed from CE2 to CE3b after albendazole treatment (Fig. 1). Based on the comparison of pathology samples sent from both liver and intramuscular CE; the albendazole has been found to leave the laminar membrane intact, degenerate the germinative membrane, thereby reducing the intra-vesicle pressure. The scolex structures were observed in the material sent from the liver, but not in the specimen sent from muscular tissue after the use of albendazole (Fig. 3).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 44-year-old Turkish woman presented with a 10-year history of a right thigh mass that enlarged over the preceding few months.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient had a longstanding swelling in her right thigh for 10 years that enlarged over recent months. Four months prior to current presentation, she had been diagnosed with multiple right lobe hepatic hydatid cysts (20-50 mm) and underwent partial hepatic cystectomy and povidone-iodine washout followed by three 1-month cycles of oral albendazole (10 mg/kg/day separated by 14-day intervals), after which she presented for definitive excision of the right thigh mass.
subjective.past_medical_history: Underwent partial hepatic cystectomy 4 months earlier for right lobe hepatic cystic echinococcosis followed by 3 cycles of oral albendazole.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for right thigh mass. Recent medication: oral albendazole (10 mg/kg/day for three 1-month cycles).

objective.physical_examination: A large palpable mass along the anterolateral aspect of the proximal and middle thirds of the right thigh.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count and serum biochemical tests were within normal limits.
objective.advanced_workup: Pre-albendazole right thigh MRI (4 months prior) showed a 180 x 100 x 75 mm multilocular cystic lesion (WHO stage CE2) within the right vastus lateralis muscle; repeat MRI after 3 cycles of albendazole showed shrinkage and transition to a 150 x 70 x 55 mm heterogeneous encapsulated cyst (WHO stage CE3b) with degenerated internal vesicles. Intact total pericystectomy via a 20-cm anterolateral thigh incision revealed dense caseified hydatid sand and daughter cysts; histopathology confirmed intramuscular cystic echinococcosis with an intact laminated membrane, degenerated germinative membrane, and absence of viable scolices (whereas the prior hepatic specimen contained viable scolices).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Intramuscular cystic echinococcosis of the right vastus lateralis muscle (150 x 70 x 55 mm) synchronous with previously resected right lobe hepatic cystic echinococcosis, confirmed by MRI (transition from WHO CE2 to CE3b on albendazole) and postoperative histopathology demonstrating an intact laminated membrane and albendazole-induced degeneration of the germinative membrane and scolices. Following intact total surgical excision, the patient completed 2 additional months of postoperative oral albendazole (10 mg/kg/day).
